S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
examples: Feels uncomfortable and restless as if something is squirming inside when sitting still.
Feels internally anxious and stifled in situations requiring prolonged sitting.
A sense of urgency and anxiety that one must keep moving or doing something.
Feels unable to endure staying still and must constantly be doing something.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
examples: Unable to engage in calm activities for long, such as reading quietly or drawing.
Cannot play quietly, often shouting or making loud noises during games or play.
Unable to stay quiet in quiet places like libraries or movie theaters, making noise.
Cannot endure and avoids quiet and calm activities like meditation or yoga.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
examples: Constantly moving and active as if driven by a motor.
Starts another task immediately after finishing one, without resting for a moment.
Unable to stay still even on weekends or days off, constantly doing something.
Appears to others to be always busy and bustling about.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
examples: Raises hand or blurts out the answer before the question is even finished in class or meetings.
Jumps to conclusions and speaks before the other person finishes their sentence.
Answers hastily without reading the question to the end in quizzes or exams.
Interrupts and answers in the middle of a conversation without listening to the other person until the end.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
examples: Cannot wait and cuts in line or gets impatient when standing in a queue.
Rushes or cuts in without waiting for their turn in games or board games.
Keeps checking the time or complaining when waiting for their turn at hospitals or public offices.
Fidgets, complains, or gets annoyed in situations where waiting for a turn is required.

symptom.disease_info: Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder, Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation, is characterized by persistent hyperactivity and impulsivity that are developmentally inappropriate, present across settings, and associated with functional impairment. In adults and older adults it may appear less as overt running or climbing and more as marked inner restlessness, excessive activity, difficulty engaging quietly, interrupting, blurting, and trouble waiting. It is distinguished from episodic mood states or situational agitation by its chronic course and cross-situational pattern rather than discrete episodes.

patient.stressor_event: Major change in financial state (e.g., a lot worse or better off than usual)
patient.stressor: After Cynthia Payton’s fixed income was strained by rising insurance costs and unexpected home repairs, she took on extra volunteer responsibilities at the senior center, including helping organize an art exhibit and small fundraising events. During the following 1 year and 5 months, long-familiar traits that friends had once viewed as spirited creativity became more noticeable: she had trouble sitting through planning meetings, often jumped in before others finished speaking, and grew visibly impatient during sign-up lines, supply distribution, and group activities. The difficulties caused embarrassment and a few strained exchanges but did not seriously disrupt her independence, church involvement, or art life. Cynthia brought the issue up herself during a primary-care visit after a wellness lecture on attention problems in older adults, and she was referred for psychiatric assessment.

S012.name: Feeling_Restless
S012.description: Often runs about or climbs in situations where it is inappropriate. (Note: In adolescents or adults, may be limited to feeling restless.)
S012.manifestation: When I'm at the senior center meetings or sitting through church announcements, I get this ants-in-my-chair feeling and have to shift around, stand up for coffee, or straighten papers just to get through it.

S013.name: Quiet_Activity_Difficulty
S013.description: Often unable to play or engage in leisure activities quietly.
S013.manifestation: Even during the art group, if everyone is supposed to be quietly painting or looking over sketches, I find myself humming, tapping my brush, or making little comments before I realize I'm disturbing the calm.

S014.name: Constant_Activity
S014.description: Is often 'on the go', acting as if 'driven by a motor'.
S014.manifestation: What brings me in is that for the past year or so I feel like I’m always puttering, fixing, arranging, or volunteering for one more thing, and even at 87 I have a hard time just sitting down and being still.

S016.name: Blurting_Answers
S016.description: Often blurts out an answer before a question has been completed.
S016.manifestation: In planning meetings for the exhibit, I’ll answer or offer my idea before the other person has finished explaining, and then I feel embarrassed because I can see I’ve stepped on their words.

S017.name: Waiting_Turn_Difficulty
S017.description: Often has difficulty waiting his or her turn.
S017.manifestation: Waiting in the sign-up line or for supplies to be handed out makes me fidgety and short, and I catch myself sighing, checking my watch, or edging forward when I really should just wait my turn.

add_requirements.Onset prior to age 12 years: I remember getting scolded in grade school for popping out of my seat, talking over classmates, and being told I was 'too lively' long before I was a teenager.
add_requirements.functional_impairment: At the senior center, I’ve had to apologize after meetings, and one friend suggested I take a smaller role at the sign-up table because my manner was making things tense.
add_requirements.duration: It has been especially noticeable for about a year and five months, since the insurance bills and home repairs pushed me into taking on more at the senior center.
